canonical_record.label: Kurvers spatial producer-scrounger evolutionary simulation
canonical_record.summary: Kurvers and colleagues modeled group foraging with a spatially explicit genetic algorithm whose simulated agents could alternate between producing and scrounging; the exploration level and the probability of scrounging were distinct, evolving continuous traits each ranging from 0 to 1.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

statement: Kurvers and colleagues modeled group foraging with a spatially explicit genetic algorithm whose simulated agents could alternate between producing and scrounging; the exploration level and the probability of scrounging were distinct, evolving continuous traits each ranging from 0 to 1.

scope.population: Simulated agents in a spatial producer-scrounger foraging game
scope.time: 2012 publication; tactics alternated within foraging rounds and genetic traits evolved across rounds
scope.assumptions: Exploration is a level or score affecting spatial movement and social attraction, not itself defined as the probability of exploring; scrounging probability governs tactic selection.
scope.uncertainty: Computational model rather than direct animal observation; outcomes depend on implemented spatial and selection assumptions.
scope.units: Dimensionless exploration level and scrounging probability, each on [0,1]
scope.quantifiers: Both traits continuous and evolvable; no fixed producer/scrounger or fast/slow types were imposed initially.

support.quote:
Here we incorporated travel times for scroungers and allowed individuals to play a mixed strategy by alternating between producer and scrounger within rounds. Importantly, we did not start with
a priori
differences between individuals by introducing fast and slow explorers in the model, or by assigning fixed foraging strategies (either producing, or scrounging) to individuals. Both the level of exploration and the scrounging probability were on a continuous scale (0–1) and were allowed to evolve (i.e., not fixed).

An individual’s strategy was encoded in a 2-locus real-valued chromosome, with locus 1 coding for the probability of scrounging P
S_I
and locus 2 coding for the value of exploration E
I
. Both loci ranged from 0 to 1

canonical_record.label: Foraging patch density shifts exploration and scrounging in simulation
canonical_record.summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, increasing food-patch density favored higher exploration; it also reduced scrounging at low or intermediate patch richness, but this reduction disappeared at high patch richness.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

statement: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, increasing food-patch density favored higher exploration; it also reduced scrounging at low or intermediate patch richness, but this reduction disappeared at high patch richness.

scope.population: Spatial genetic-algorithm producer-scrounger simulations with varying food-patch density and richness
scope.time: 2012 model runs; evolved outcomes averaged over the last 10 rounds
scope.assumptions: Effect conditional on richness for scrounging; exploration denotes evolved movement tendency, not a probability of exploring.
scope.uncertainty: Model-specific result; no estimated universal response for natural animals.
scope.units: Qualitative direction of simulated evolved exploration levels and scrounging probabilities
scope.quantifiers: Density effect on scrounging only for low/intermediate richness, not high richness.

support.quote: An increase in patch density led to an increase in exploration and a reduction in scrounging, but the latter only under conditions of low/intermediate patch richness. An increase in patch richness resulted in increased scrounging, but there was no effect on exploration levels.

canonical_record.label: Food patch richness increases modeled scrounging
canonical_record.summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, richer food patches increased evolved scrounging propensities among both fast and slow explorers, while patch richness showed no effect on evolved exploration.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

statement: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, richer food patches increased evolved scrounging propensities among both fast and slow explorers, while patch richness showed no effect on evolved exploration.

scope.population: Spatial genetic-algorithm simulated foragers, across modeled exploration levels
scope.assumptions: Patch richness refers to the number of food items per patch rather than patch density; fast/slow explorers refer to trait values.
scope.uncertainty: Null richness effect on exploration pertains to investigated simulation settings, not all ecological environments.
scope.units: Qualitative evolved scrounging probability and exploration level
scope.quantifiers: Richness effect on scrounging at both fast and slow exploration values; no observed effect on exploration.

canonical_record.label: No stable explorer-type polymorphism within simulated environments
canonical_record.summary: In the Kurvers evolutionary simulations, populations within a given environmental run approached one exploration optimum rather than retaining a stable coexistence of distinct explorer personality types.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

statement: In the Kurvers evolutionary simulations, populations within a given environmental run approached one exploration optimum rather than retaining a stable coexistence of distinct explorer personality types.

scope.population: Populations of simulated agents within individual evolutionary runs under a fixed environmental parameter combination
scope.assumptions: Intra-run convergence is distinct from variation across different simulation environments.
scope.uncertainty: No observed within-run stable coexistence under modeled conditions does not preclude it in real animals or different models.
scope.units: Qualitative evolutionary outcome for simulated exploration level
scope.quantifiers: Within a given run, rather than all runs or populations universally.

canonical_record.label: Thornton meerkat provisioning and monitoring sample sizes
canonical_record.summary: Thornton analyzed 1,070 scorpion feeds by 347 meerkat helpers to 339 pups from 137 litters in 15 groups for prey-provisioning state, and recorded monitoring times for 6,148 feeds by 300 helpers to 244 pups from 65 litters in 13 groups.

canonical_record.summary: In Thornton’s meerkat scorpion-provisioning analysis, older eligible helpers were more likely to give pups intact scorpions, whereas prior experience with earlier foraging litters showed no statistically significant association after controlling for helper age.

canonical_record.label: Meerkat pup monitoring varies with prey movement size and pup age
canonical_record.summary: For 6,148 observed meerkat pup feeds, helpers spent longer monitoring pups when provisioned prey was moving or larger and spent less time monitoring as pups grew older.

canonical_record.label: Meerkat monitoring duration declines with nearby helpers and rain
canonical_record.summary: In Thornton’s meerkat feeding observations, pup monitoring duration decreased with larger litter size, higher recent rainfall, and the presence of another helper within two metres.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

statement: In Thornton’s meerkat feeding observations, pup monitoring duration decreased with larger litter size, higher recent rainfall, and the presence of another helper within two metres.

scope.quantifiers: Declines with increasing litter size and rainfall and if another helper is present within 2 m.
